items.title: Further Scaling Our Malaria Grantmaking
items.summary: GiveWell says it expects to grant over $1 billion this year, more than double the $418 million committed in 2025. It aims to grant at least $2.5 billion in new malaria funding from 2027 through 2032, potentially several times that amount, possibly to existing and new organizations.

items.title: The $18 billion Ford Foundation is getting its biggest overhaul since 2015 to fight autocracy—with about $700 million in grants expected in 2027
items.summary: Fortune reports that the Ford Foundation, valued at $18 billion, is undergoing its biggest overhaul since 2015 to fight autocracy. About $700 million in grants is expected in 2027.

items.title: What’s happening with Section 504—and how are nonprofits fighting?
items.summary: On September 23, 2026, a federal court in Texas v. Kennedy removed six HHS regulatory provisions on community-integration rights for people with disabilities, applying nationally. Advocates say nonprofits are mobilizing, and more than 8.4 million Medicaid beneficiaries received home- and community-based services in 2023.

items.title: Ford Foundation Unveils 7-Point Funding Realignment
items.summary: The Ford Foundation unveiled a new strategic direction focused on protecting democratic values, fundamental freedoms, and inclusive economies worldwide. The item is a short excerpt from the announcement.

items.title: Veteran charities are highly visible but get less than 1 percent of U.S. giving
items.summary: A Lilly Family School of Philanthropy report finds donations to military and veteran charities rose 5.9 percent in 2024 to about $4 billion, with the top 10 recipients capturing 85 percent of growth. Their share of U.S. giving was 0.68 percent in 2024.

items.title: Ford’s ‘absolutely seismic’ reboot comes into focus
items.summary: Heather Gerken's first strategy overhaul as Ford Foundation president will focus the grantmaker on strengthening democracy and economic opportunity. Trustees approved reducing program areas from 19 to seven and increasing the number and size of multiyear grants.

items.title: The Ford Foundation will throw more weight behind democracy
items.summary: The Ford Foundation will overhaul spending, with seven new programs covering democratic governance, inclusive economies, trustworthy information, public safety, gender equality, global cooperation, and racial justice. The $18 billion endowment reorientation follows Heather Gerken's first year as president.

items.title: What happens when a fiscal sponsor shuts down?
items.summary: The High Desert Community Foundation will end its fiscal sponsorship program on December 31, 2026, with operations ceasing by June 2027. The program supports more than 30 community projects, which must now form independent nonprofits or find another fiscal sponsor.

items.title: Who fills the gap when philanthropy walks away from social justice movements?
items.summary: Several major foundations have recently and quietly wound down funding for social justice areas including immigration, LGBTQ+ rights, reproductive justice, and racial justice. The piece calls on the sector to organize a new path forward for sustaining social justice work.

items.title: The tax-subsidized shrug: How foundation leaders threaten democracy and the nonprofit sector
items.summary: Discusses a Center for Effective Philanthropy report based on survey responses from nearly 200 foundation CEOs. It states that 98 percent acknowledge foundations need to change, but only 14 percent think change is very likely, and most have not raised payouts above the 5 percent minimum.

items.title: Money worries cloud voter mobilization efforts
items.summary: The Voter Participation Center ran a $40 million midterm turnout campaign after funding arrived late. The center aims to help 500,000 people submit voter registrations and 400,000 vote-by-mail applications, and it has received donor-advised fund and foundation support.

items.title: Podcast: Is Philanthropy Fueling Polarization?
items.summary: A Chronicle of Philanthropy podcast features Daniel Stid of the American Enterprise Institute and Phil Buchanan of the Center for Effective Philanthropy debating whether philanthropic funding of national policy advocacy has deepened polarization. They also discuss the nonprofit sector's dependence on federal funding and the breakdown of the bipartisan consensus supporting it.

items.title: A nonprofit bought a grocery market to fund survivor recovery—can the model deliver?

items.title: Why direct mail still delivers at year-end in the age of AI
